class_id: a nightly audit that aborts on one check's error, read by a delta consumer that counts not-run checks as resolved
feature: any nightly multi-check audit run against a database whose migrations lag the audit code (production between releases), together with the consumer that diffs its output day over day
symptom: one check queries a column or table that the target database does not have yet; the error is not caught per check, so the whole run aborts and every later check silently never runs. The day-over-day consumer compares check ids present yesterday with ids present today and reports the missing ones as GONE, the same word it uses for a failure that was fixed, and prints 'no new findings'. The audit therefore goes blind and announces an improvement at the same moment. Wider shape: a diff that cannot tell 'absent' from 'passed' turns any crash of its producer into good news.
